brief: Goldman one-delta desk head Rich Privorotsky argues the S&P/Nasdaq are near another breakout, and expects the rally to stay poorly subscribed since most investors spent September arguing it couldn't work. He flags seasonality, still-high real rates and a geopolitical left tail as headwinds, and notes the current half-month is the worst seasonal stretch of the year. His optimism rests on "agentic disruption": Muse is proof of distribution, not the endpoint, and AI agents are set to sharply cut friction between people, technology and capital, which he calls the best expression of that shift for equities. As large corporates underwrite the safety, infrastructure and distribution AI agents need, proliferation should expand rapidly, letting friction and rent-seeking fall away from the economy and capital redeploy more productively. He calls the aggregate effect positive for equities and structurally disinflationary, though winners and losers take months to years to sort out. For now the trade runs through the CPU/semis chain, with TSMC near its highs. Financials were notably weak even as tech pushed higher, a divergence he flags as a second-derivative signal.
